references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Most food businesses that sell food to the public must register with the Health Protection Service before opening, including non-profit community organisations such as school canteens. Apply online through the ACT Government smart form or lodge the Food Business - Registration Application by email to hps@act.gov.au. ACT Health inspects the premises before registration is granted. All registered food businesses must nominate an appropriately trained food safety supervisor (some non-profit community organisations are exempt). The registration certificate must be displayed. Food transport vehicles registered in another state and businesses that only transport food are exempt. Contact 02 5124 9700.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Fees depend on the risk classification and the length of registration: 1 year $163.00 (low risk), $239.50 (medium), $321.55 (high); 2 years $326.00, $479.00, $643.10; 3 years $489.00, $718.50, $964.65. Businesses that supply food while providing services (hospitals, licensed childcare, parent-run school canteens) and some community organisations are exempt. The risk classification section of the application form sets the category.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Licence types include general, on (bar, nightclub, and restaurant and cafe subclasses), off, club, special, caterer's and micro-producer off licences. Apply on the Application for liquor licence form, in person at an Access Canberra Service Centre or online through the Liquor Licence Enquiry form. A risk assessment management plan is needed where liquor is consumed on the premises (not for off licences or restaurants and cafes unless asked). Everyone serving liquor and crowd controllers need current RSA certification. Attach approved plans and certificates of occupancy, police checks issued within 3 months for each person named, and a provision of lease advice certificate. Access Canberra publishes a public notice and gives you a sign to display during a 30-day consultation. Approval can take up to 90 days. Phone 13 22 81.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Employers must hold a current workers' compensation policy for all their workers in the ACT, including Pty Ltd companies with one or more workers. Workers include anyone under a contract of service, and a contractor who works on a regular and systematic basis is deemed a worker. Operating without cover brings penalties, payment of the avoided premium and up to double the avoided premium for up to five years. Employers keep an injury register on site, display a notice with the insurer's name and policy details, and give the insurer written notice of an injury within 48 hours.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] From 1 July 2026 the ACT payroll tax threshold is $1.75 million a year ($145,833.33 a month), down from $2 million. 2026-27 rates: 6.75% for Australia-wide wages over $1.75 million up to $20 million, rising in steps to 8.75% over $150 million. Employers must apply to register within seven days after the end of the month they go over the threshold, using the online payroll tax registration notification form. Returns are monthly (due the 7th, December's by 14 January) with an annual reconciliation due 28 July, lodged through the Self Service Portal.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Construction occupations are licensed under the Construction Occupations (Licensing) Act 2004, with applications handled by Access Canberra's Construction and Workplace Licensing team. Builder licences: Class A (unlimited height), Class B (up to 3 storeys), Class C (up to 2 storeys for Class 1, 2 or 10a buildings and some Class 10b structures) and Class D (non-structural basic building work); demolition and pool installation need endorsements. Electricians have six licence classes; plumbers, drainers and gasfitters have several classes. Apply on the online forms for an individual builder (formCode 1707), electrician (1715), plumber, drainer, gasfitter and gas appliance worker (1716), or company or partnership (1295). First-time Class A, B or C builders must pass the ACT Regulatory Assessment at CIT (80% pass mark). Fees are set by the annual fee determination. Builder applications take at least 4 weeks; prioritised electrician and plumbing applications about 3 weeks. The licence is on the public register within 7 days of paying the term fee. Criminal history checks older than 6 months aren't accepted. Contact 02 6207 8096, cwpl@act.gov.au.
references.interpretation: Building, electrical, plumbing, drainage and gasfitting work in the ACT needs a construction occupation licence. Captured on 2026-10-12 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A vehicle must be registered to be driven in the ACT; an unregistered vehicle is uninsured. Register in person at an Access Canberra Service Centre with proof of identity, after a roadworthy inspection where required. A private applicant completes the application to establish registration on the back of the vehicle inspection report. You choose a Motor Accident Injuries (MAI) insurer (AAMI, APIA, GIO or NRMA) and pay registration, MAI and stamp duty of 1.5% of the purchase price or market value, whichever is higher, by card. Registration can be for 3, 6 or 12 months. Phone 13 22 81.

outcomes.title: Get the vehicle inspected at Hume, then register it at an Access Canberra Service Centre
outcomes.detail: A vehicle being registered in Australia for the first time must be inspected at the Access Canberra Motor Vehicle Inspection Station in Hume, by appointment (call 13 22 81). Personal imports and vehicles over 25 years old can use any authorised inspection station. Drive it there on an unregistered vehicle permit. A light vehicle inspection costs $89.20 in 2026-27. Then take the inspection report (fill in the registration application on the back) and your ID to an Access Canberra Service Centre within a month. Choose a Motor Accident Injuries insurer and pay registration, MAI and stamp duty of 1.5% of the price or market value, whichever is higher.

approval.pathway: Inspection at Hume, then register in person

payload.task: Book an inspection at Hume and register the vehicle with Access Canberra

outcomes.title: Selling vehicles as a business needs a motor vehicle dealer licence
outcomes.detail: In the ACT anyone who buys, sells or exchanges motor vehicles as a business needs a licence from Access Canberra. Lodge the ACT motor vehicle dealer licence application online with two proof of identity documents and a name-only police check for each person (plus an ASIC extract for a company). The 2026-27 fee is $891.00 for 1 year or $4,037.00 for 5 years.

rule_sets.title: ACT: boat registration and licences
rule_sets.description: The ACT has no boat registration or licence scheme; ACT boat owners register and license in another state, and ACT lakes have their own permits.
limitations: Built from the Access Canberra 'Boating on ACT lakes' page; NSW registration and licence rules were not read.
Doesn't cover National Capital Authority approvals in detail.
Not legal advice. Check with Access Canberra (13 22 81) or the NSW agency before you rely on it.

rules.title: No ACT boat registration or licence
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-12), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: The ACT doesn't register boats or license drivers: use NSW or another state
outcomes.detail: The ACT Government has no boat registration or licence scheme. A power boat used on ACT lakes must be registered in an Australian state or territory, and you need that state's boat licence. If you will use the boat on NSW waters, register and license it with NSW. In the ACT, power boats are allowed on Lake Ginninderra, Lake Tuggeranong, Kingston Harbour and the Molonglo River above Lake Burley Griffin; going faster than 10 knots needs an ACT authorisation. The National Capital Authority approves powered boats on Lake Burley Griffin, and Googong Reservoir needs a free ACT boating permit.

payload.task: Register and license the boat in NSW or another state
